name: Minced rather than intact beef in the tested older-adult meal
context: Ten older men received 135 g of intrinsically phenylalanine-labelled beef, as mince or intact steak, in a randomized crossover. Minced beef produced faster dietary phenylalanine appearance and greater six-hour dietary phenylalanine availability. Muscle protein synthesis did not differ detectably.

name: Boiled rather than raw eggs in the tested postexercise meal
context: In a 45-man post-resistance-exercise trial, five boiled whole eggs produced higher peak plasma essential amino acids than five raw whole eggs. Muscle protein synthesis did not differ significantly between the egg groups. Heat-induced protein denaturation was a proposed explanation and was not measured as a mediator.

name: Sleep after learning
context: Sleep can support formation, selective retention, removal and resizing of connections after learning. Mouse sleep/REM manipulations and ultrastructure differ by age, region and endpoint. More spines is not always better; no universal human sleep duration is derived.

name: Steam spinach or broccoli rather than boiling in the tested conditions
context: Preserves dietary folate upstream of the admitted folate-to-5-MTHF substrate supply for methionine synthase; no measured remethylation response. Controlled food-composition experiment, not a feeding trial. Total folate is not a 5-MTHF quantity. No absorption, tissue flux or clinical outcome was measured; other foods and preparation objectives differ.

name: Tested malted and soaked oat porridge
context: Higher fractional zinc absorption than matched untreated-oat porridge; upstream provision of admitted catalytic zinc, not measured BHMT activity. Pilot-plant malting and controlled soaking are not household overnight oats; acute absorption in ten adults does not establish tissue BHMT flux, long-term zinc status or clinical benefit.

name: Ten-week high-fermented-food dietary pattern
context: 18 analysed per arm, generally healthy adults; four-week ramp to about six fermented-food servings/day and six-week maintenance; high-fibre active comparator, no usual-diet control. Two participants entered the high-fibre arm by request without randomisation. Serial immune profiling with multiple-testing corrections. 19/93 serum proteins decreased, including IL-6, IL-10 and IL-12b; microbiota diversity increased as a separate endpoint. The study team was unblinded. The serum protein findings were exploratory, the primary cytokine-response score was null, and microbiota mediation remains unresolved.

name: Tested fibre/fruit-rich mixed meal versus the high-fat/high-carbohydrate comparison
context: NF-kB DNA-binding activity rose after the tested high-fat/high-carbohydrate meal but not after the isocaloric fibre/fruit-rich comparison. NF-kB DNA-binding activity rose after the tested high-fat/high-carbohydrate meal but not after the isocaloric fibre/fruit-rich comparison. The mechanism of that difference was not isolated. Two groups of ten healthy lean adults ate one of two 910-kcal meals. The meals differed in several foods and macronutrients, and random allocation was not described. CRP and TNF-α did not change.

name: Limit unnecessary cumulative heat exposure when retaining creatine in pork products
context: Controlled pork-loin and cooked-ham experiments found greater creatine-to-creatinine conversion with higher heat exposure, especially at the product surface. Evidence is limited to processed pork matrices and does not establish higher creatine intake or cerebral target engagement.

name: Aerobic or resistance training
context: Twelve weeks of aerobic or resistance training increased skeletal-muscle NAMPT protein, the enzyme that limits nicotinamide salvage, in young and older adults. The study measured NAMPT protein, not NAD⁺ concentration. Adipose NAMPT did not change after high-intensity interval training. Attention and cognitive energy were not measured.

name: Include dietary fat with provitamin-A vegetables
context: Include some dietary fat with provitamin-A vegetables to support carotenoid absorption. Dietary fat supports absorption of vegetable provitamin-A carotenoids upstream of the vitamin A–retinoid biology recorded for this PM. Measured carotenoid absorption, not vitamin A conversion, intestinal retinoic-acid delivery or improved tight-junction function. Applies to the tested vegetable meal; do not generalise to every fat-soluble compound, impose the study fat dose, or promise reduced permeability.

name: Reduce alcohol exposure
context: Reducing alcohol exposure can remove a barrier stressor; documented recovery concerns patients with alcohol dependence and elevated permeability. Reducing ethanol exposure removes a demonstrated epithelial barrier stressor; recovery during abstinence is documented in alcohol-dependent patients with elevated permeability. Recovery evidence concerns alcohol-dependent patients with elevated permeability, not every drinker. Abstinence was part of detoxification rather than a randomised isolated intervention. The acute trial delivered ethanol intraduodenally; ordinary drinking patterns and long-term symptoms were not tested.

name: Tested fibre/fruit-rich mixed meal versus the high-fat/high-carbohydrate comparison
context: The meal comparison measured different acute plasma endotoxin/LBP responses. In a small acute comparison of two 910-kcal meals in healthy lean adults, endotoxin and LPS-binding protein rose after the high-fat/high-carbohydrate meal and did not rise significantly after the fibre- and fruit-rich meal. The meals differed in multiple components, and these endpoints do not directly measure gut permeability.

name: Fish before rice in the studied meal sequence
context: Fish first delayed gastric emptying, an upstream control of carbohydrate delivery. An acute meal result; no claim that protein alone accounts for the effect.

name: Cooling and reheating the tested chickpea pasta
context: Cooling and reheating increased measured resistant starch in this pasta, reducing the readily digestible fraction as a plausible entry-pathway change. Twelve healthy adults; 24 h at 4 °C and the tested reheating method. Glucose entry was not measured and digestible carbohydrate was not re-matched after processing.

name: Early eating with front-loaded calories (six-day trial)
context: 10 adults with prediabetes and overweight/obesity. Six days of matched weight-maintenance food: 08:00-16:00, 80% of calories before 14:00, versus usual later distribution; randomised crossover without washout. In a small prediabetes crossover, the tested early, front-loaded eating schedule reduced mean amplitude of glycaemic excursions (MAGE) over six days versus later calorie distribution; mean glucose and several other variability/range measures were inconclusive. Small sample, no washout; timing, eating-window length and calorie distribution cannot be separated.

name: Supervised interval walking (two-week trial)
context: 14 adults with type 2 diabetes; 13 usable CGM records. Randomised crossover: ten supervised 60-minute sessions over two weeks, alternating three-minute slower/faster walking; continuous and inactive comparator periods, multiweek washout. Two weeks of the tested supervised interval-walking programme reduced mean amplitude of glycaemic excursions (MAGE) versus an inactive control period in a small type 2 diabetes crossover trial. Small unmasked trial, baseline imbalance and missing sensor record; oxidative-stress markers did not improve. No blanket superiority to all continuous exercise.

name: Slow-paced breathing at six cycles per minute
context: The tested breathing pace increased during-session RMSSD, a cardiac vagal-associated measure. Session HRV is respiration-dependent and does not show durable whole-body vagal improvement.
